title: CONSUMABLE SALES
content:
A consumable is a product that gets used up, depleted, or replaced through normal use. That creates the possibility of repeat purchases, but it does not automatically create recurring income for you.

The key question is what happens when the customer needs more. Do they return to your business? Does a company continue attributing that customer to you? Do you have to win the sale again? Does another seller capture the reorder?

PRODUCT REPEAT IS NOT SELLER REPEAT
Coffee, supplements, skincare, pet food, cleaning products, and printer ink can all be repurchased. But a product being naturally replenishable does not tell you whether YOU receive the next sale.

That distinction matters when comparing ownership, reselling, affiliate programs, and network/direct-sales structures.

AUTOSHIP DOES NOT CHANGE THE PRODUCT TYPE
A customer may choose automatic replenishment for a consumable. That can make ordering more convenient, but the underlying value is still the physical product being consumed. This is different from a subscription whose core value is continued access, membership, software, content, or ongoing support.

WHAT TO DECIDE NEXT
Do you want the consumable product itself to be yours, or do you want to sell an existing consumable product owned by another company?

I WANT MY OWN CONSUMABLE PRODUCT → PDF 21.
I WANT TO SELL AN EXISTING CONSUMABLE PRODUCT → PDF 26.

WHY CONSUMABLES DESERVE THEIR OWN BRANCH

A one-off physical product can create additional sales, but the original item may last for years. A consumable is different because normal use itself creates another potential buying event.

That can be attractive, but it also creates a temptation to treat repeat consumption as guaranteed recurring revenue. It is not. Customers can switch products, stop using the category, buy elsewhere, cancel automatic orders, or simply forget. The seller may also lose attribution depending on the business arrangement.

So this branch keeps two questions visible at the same time:
1. Is this a product people naturally need again?
2. What mechanism, if any, connects the repeat purchase back to your business?

EXAMPLE

Imagine a customer buys a 30-serving supplement. The product may run out in about a month. That tells you something about the product's consumption cycle. It does not tell you whether the customer will reorder, whether they will reorder from the same seller, or whether the seller receives compensation on the reorder. Those are separate facts.

WHERE TO GO NEXT
If you want to own the consumable product, continue to PDF 21. If you want to sell an existing consumable, continue to PDF 26.
